stem.en: Suppose the skin cells near a cut started dividing by meiosis instead of mitosis. What do you think would happen to the cut?

text.en: It would heal much faster, because each dividing cell gives four new cells.

feedback.en: Four cells with half the chromosomes are not normal skin cells.

text.en: It would heal in the usual way, because any new cell will do.

feedback.en: New skin cells need the full set of chromosomes.

text.en: It would not heal normally: new cells would have half the number.

feedback.en: Yes. Repair needs cells with the same chromosomes as the parent.

text.en: Nothing would change, as meiosis and mitosis give the same cells.

feedback.en: Meiosis gives cells with half the number of chromosomes.

explanation.en: Repair needs daughter cells with the same DNA as the parent. Meiosis would give cells with half the chromosomes, so the cut would not heal normally.

hints.en: How many chromosomes does each cell get from meiosis?
